arts-languages-review.json.scope: One original focused module per official unit/theme, with distinct original four-part arts portfolio and five-part Capstone skill sequences. This is not exhaustive syllabus coverage or College Board approval.
sourceChecks: Each listed official AP Students URL opened or resolved through official search on 15 October 2026.
Modern languages use the six revised 2026-27 themes. AP Central explicitly confirms fall 2026 effective date and January 2027 release of project packet.
Latin uses the current six-unit Pliny/Vergil sequence, revised for fall 2025. Original Latin exercises are not assigned passages.
Business has five numbered units, with separate part 1 and part 2 within Unit 3, producing six modules. Correct official slug is business-personal-finance.
Cybersecurity has five current units. Exercises are fictional and defensive; no operational probing is required.
Art portfolios use an original skill sequence rather than invented official units. Current 2026-27 submission and AI requirements are deferred to official guidance.
Music has eight units; Art History ten; Spanish Literature eight. Capstone pages describe five big ideas, mapped here to original skill sequences.
contentBoundaries: Subject-expert and native-speaker review remains pending; structural validation is not subject approval.
No authentic audio, speech recording, score rendering, studio work or portfolio assessment is implemented by these JSON lessons.
Art History hypothetical scenarios teach analytical methods but do not supply the required image set.
Spanish Literature and Latin original passages do not replace required readings.
Modern-language fictional scenarios are not authentic sources for the required project.
Capstone exercises do not collect participants, perform studies or fabricate findings.
Financial examples are hypothetical arithmetic, not personalised financial advice.
No deployment or full build performed by this content worker.
